Quotes about feeling

Philosophy Quotes About Grief, Death & Loss

Grief exposes what we valued. Philosophers of death, suffering, and consolation ask how to mourn without denial, and how suffering can clarify—or distort—our sense of the good.

Quotes / About / Grief

26 quotations on grief

  1. It is worse to do injustice than to suffer it.
    Socrates
    Justice
  2. Death is nothing to us: for what has been dissolved has no sensation, and what has no sensation is nothing to us.
    Epicurus
    Death
  3. Pleasure is the beginning and end of the happy life — not the pleasures of profligates, but freedom from pain in the body and from disturbance in the soul.
    Epicurus
    Life
  4. There are more things that frighten us than crush us, and we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
    Seneca
    Fear
  5. He who has learned how to die has unlearned how to be a slave.
    Seneca
    Death
  6. Do not act as if you were going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over you. While you live, while it is in your power, be good.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Philosophy
  7. If you are distressed by anything external, it is not the thing itself that disturbs you, but your own judgment about it.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Judgment
  8. Therefore death is nothing to us, and does not concern us at all.
    Lucretius
    Death
  9. To philosophize is to learn how to die.
    Michel de Montaigne
    Death
  10. Depart then in peace; the one who releases you is also at peace.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Death
  11. This very practice of philosophers is a release and separation of soul from body.
    Plato
    Philosophy
  12. From the very fountain of delights rises something bitter that chokes among the flowers themselves.
    Lucretius
    Desire
  13. Before joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are issued, that is called the Mean; when issued and all hit due measure, that is called Harmony.
    The Doctrine of the Mean
    Order
  14. Contacts with the senses give cold and heat, pleasure and pain; they come and go and are impermanent—endure them.
    Bhagavad Gita
    Philosophy
  15. All life is suffering.
    Arthur Schopenhauer
    Philosophy
  16. A free man thinks of nothing less than of death.
    Baruch Spinoza
    Freedom
  17. Three passions, simple but overwhelmingly strong, have governed my life: the longing for love, the search for knowledge, and unbearable pity for the suffering of mankind.
    Bertrand Russell
    Love
  18. Treating pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same…
    Bhagavad Gita
    Equanimity
  19. There is no greater pain than to recall happy times in misery.
    Dante Alighieri
    Memory
  20. Contacts with the senses, O son of Kunti, give cold and heat, pleasure and pain; they come and go — endure them.
    Bhagavad Gita
    Endurance
  21. Nature has placed mankind under the governance of two sovereign masters, pain and pleasure.
    Jeremy Bentham
    Life
  22. For everything you have missed, you have gained something else; and for everything you gain, you lose something else.
    Ralph Waldo Emerson
    Philosophy
  23. The world has kissed my soul with its pain, asking for its return in songs.
    Rabindranath Tagore
    Philosophy
  24. The human mind, insofar as it is a simple substance distinct from the body, can neither suffer from the body nor be confused with it, but by itself, according to its own operations, understands and wills.
    Anton Wilhelm Amo
    Mind
  25. To love a being is to say: thou, thou shalt not die.
    Gabriel Marcel
    Love
  26. Jingjie is not a matter of scenery alone: joy, anger, sorrow, and happiness are also realms of the human heart. Whoever can write true scenery and true feeling may be said to have jingjie.
    Wang Guowei
    Beauty
